hints: Think about what happens to the row and column indices.
The value at matrix[r][c] belongs at result[c][r].
The transpose has n rows and m columns.
Fill the result directly instead of trying to transpose in place.
title: Transpose Matrix Problem

notes: The matrix is guaranteed to be non-empty and rectangular.
Transposition exchanges row and column positions: result[c][r] = matrix[r][c].
A rectangular matrix changes shape from m x n to n x m.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: The first row of the transpose contains the first column of the original matrix, and so on.
A 2 x 3 matrix becomes a 3 x 2 matrix by swapping row and column indices.

content.problemStatement:
With a 2D integer array `matrix`, output *the **transpose** of* `matrix`.

The **transpose** of a matrix is the matrix flipped over its main diagonal, switching the matrix's row and column indices.

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/02/10/hint_transpose.png)

**Example 1:**

```
Input: matrix = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]
Output: [[1,4,7],[2,5,8],[3,6,9]]
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: matrix = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]]
Output: [[1,4],[2,5],[3,6]]
```

**Constraints:**

* `m == matrix.length`
* `n == matrix[i].length`
* `1 <= m, n <= 1000`
* `1 <= m * n <= 10^5`
* `-10^9 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10^30`

notes: Expected output is the JSON-serialised matrix returned by transpose.
The input is rectangular, so every row has the same number of columns.
solution.approach: Create an output matrix with n rows and m columns, then place matrix[r][c] at result[c][r] for every cell.

better.complexity: O(m * n) time and O(m * n) space including the returned result.
better.description: Create a fresh n x m result and map each input cell directly: result[c][r] = matrix[r][c]. Each input cell is processed once.

optimal.complexity: O(m * n) time and O(m * n) space including the returned result; O(1) auxiliary space beyond it.
optimal.description: The direct index mapping result[c][r] = matrix[r][c] is asymptotically optimal because the transpose contains exactly m * n output elements, so every element must be written.

bruteForce.complexity: O((m * n) * (m + n)) time and O(m * n) output space.
bruteForce.description: For each cell of the output, scan the original matrix until the corresponding row and column are found. This demonstrates the row/column mapping but repeats work for every output cell.

solution.spaceComplexity: O(m * n) for the returned transpose (O(1) auxiliary space beyond the output).

followUps: Can the transpose be performed in place for a square matrix?
What changes when the matrix is rectangular?
How would you transpose a stream of rows without storing the full input?
